title: continuous-batcher: improve scheduler fairness, starvation prevention, and adaptive timeouts
author: Ava Chen
description: Motivation: continuous batching scheduler exhibited unfair throughput distribution under mixed-priority workloads and occasional starvation of long-tail requests. This PR introduces a set of conservative scheduler tunings and a small feature: adaptive per-priority enqueue timeouts to bound wait latency and ensure forward progress. Changes include: 1) introduction of a credit-based fairness allocator that periodically rebalances batch tokens across priority lanes to avoid starvation, 2) a new adaptive timeout heuristic that observes recent service times and inflight batch sizes to set per-priority max-wait thresholds, 3) a soft-deadline preemption path that allows batches that have been waiting beyond their adaptive timeout to be prioritized for the next tick, 4) better telemetry: new metrics (scheduler.wait_time_p50/p95/p99, scheduler.starved_count, scheduler.rebalanced_batches) and logs for debugging, 5) unit and integration tests for corner cases (rapid priority flips, sustained high-QPS with small sequence lengths), 6) small kernel-level guard rails to avoid excessive KV-cache eviction when preempting batches. Performance results: on our perf-canary harness with mixed small/medium sequences and 3-priority classes, end-to-end p99 latency for high-priority requests improved by ~18% under contention and starvation incidents were eliminated in repeated runs. Backwards compatibility: no public API changes. See linked linear tasks ENG-3421 and ENG-3489 for benchmarks and rollout plan. Checklist: [x] design review, [x] unit tests, [x] integration perf tests, [x] observability added, [x] docs note in changelog draft.

review_comments: Diego Morales: The credit allocator logic looks good; can you add a short comment explaining why we rebalance on epoch boundary instead of per-tick? I worry about oscillation.
Ava Chen: Replied that rebalance on epoch boundary reduces churn and avoids thrashing for transient spikes; added comment and a unit test that simulates oscillation and asserts stability.
Priya Nair: Please ensure the adaptive timeout uses an EWMA with a conservative alpha; observed a case in benchmarks where timeouts were too aggressive and increased tail latency.
Ava Chen: Adjusted EWMA alpha to 0.15 and ran perf-canary; updated benchmark notes in ENG-3489.
Ethan Brooks: Can KV cache guard rails cause memory pressure increases in worst-case? Add a fallback to disable preemption if memory protection triggers.
Ava Chen: Added a soft cap and a boolean flag that disables preemption when KV cache free memory falls below configured threshold; added an integration test that simulates low-memory.
Diego Morales: Approving pending CI green.
